title: Auth Control Plane transport error envelope (v1 wire format)
description:
The body auth-service's shared HTTP transport (internal/auth/httpapi) writes when it answers before any route runs: 400 (a body that could not be read), 404 (no route), 405 (method not allowed, with Allow), 413 (body over the limit), 429 (the route's rate bucket or the in-flight cap is spent, with Retry-After) and 500 (a recovered panic). A route answers error.v1; this envelope is only the transport's own (acp ruling 2026-10-19 on #4519).

Every code has ONE fixed message: the text is a compile-time constant per code (httpapi.message), so the body has no slot a path, a dependency error or a request body can reach. The message is therefore one of six fixed texts, never free text. request_id is the server-minted transport id (a UUID; auth-service never reuses a client X-Request-ID), the same value as the X-Request-ID header.

enum: this method is not allowed on this path
the request body exceeds the configured limit
too many requests for this route
the request body could not be read
the request could not be processed
message.description: The fixed text of the code (httpapi.message). The text is one of the six transport texts; which text goes with which code is the transport's constant table, which TestTransportErrorGoldensAreWhatTheTransportWrites pins against the accept fixtures.

request_id.description: The server-minted transport request id, lowercase UUID text.
